Mapping

iSAQB Foundation curriculum mapping

Level 1 follows the public topics of the iSAQB Certified Professional for Software Architecture, Foundation Level curriculum. This page shows which lessons relate to which chapters, and where we are not there yet.

Start with Level 1

Independent preparation, not an iSAQB course. This is Intellica’s own reading of the public curriculum. We are not affiliated with iSAQB and are not an accredited training provider. No Intellica course replaces or predicts the result of the external exam. Confirm the current curriculum, format and rules with a certification body.

What iSAQB publishes

Checked 2026-11-25.

Active curriculum
2025.1-rev2-EN, 38 learning goals in six chapters. Goals carry R1 (applied and examined), R2 (understood; may be examined) and R3 (context; not examined).
Exam format (iSAQB FAQ)
Roughly 40 multiple-choice questions, about 75 minutes, 60 percent of the maximum points to pass. Training is not required. Rules can change.
Next curriculum
2027.1-RC1-EN-20261113 is a release candidate. It is not final.

Practice exams

5 mock papers of 40 questions are built from an original bank of 206 questions, weighted by chapter as the curriculum is. Scoring is Intellica’s own practice scoring. The questions are not real exam questions. The readiness guide (80 percent on three different papers, no chapter below 70 percent) is Intellica guidance, not a guarantee. See Level 1.

The 2027.1 release candidate

Read 2026-11-25. It is a preview and may change before it is final.

The candidate recommends 1,050 minutes and lists these chapters:

ChapterRecommended time
1. Basic Concepts of Software Architecture120 min
2. Requirements and Constraints180 min
3. Design and Development360 min
4. Specification and Communication240 min
5. Use and Risks of Artificial Intelligence60 min
6. Examples90 min

Its AI chapter has three learning goals: Deciding on the use of AI in architecture work; Verification of AI-generated artefacts; Recognising the risks and the ethical and societal effects of AI.

Lesson 13 of Level 1 already teaches verification, provenance and risk for AI-assisted work. It is Intellica extension content and is not tagged as exam content. When the final curriculum is published we will compare it with the active one and update the lessons, bank and papers.

What is outside this mapping

  • The iSAQB Advanced level has its own modules, experience rules and a project-and-defence examination. Intellica does not prepare for it.
  • Levels 2 to 6 are Intellica programmes. They are not iSAQB courses.

Reviewed 2026-11-25. Intellica is independent of iSAQB, arc42, ISO, IEC, IEEE and the Software Engineering Institute. Mappings show how our lessons relate to published topics. They are not an affiliation, an approval or a prediction of any exam result.
